newsitem.title: USA: July foreign crude activity winds down in US Gulf.
newsitem.headline: July foreign crude activity winds down in US Gulf.

text.p: Foreign crude activity in the U.S. Gulf of Mexico began to wind down on Monday, with most foreign crudes already sold and many refiners wrapping up their July requirements, traders said.
"We're closing in but we're still looking. If we have an economic cargo shown to us, we would kick out some domestic barrels," a trader for a U.S. refining company said.
A trader usually involved in selling crude said most July cargoes were already sold. "I don't see much that's left to offer. People are starting to look to August now."
A tight transatlantic arbitrage continued to keep North Sea cargoes out of the Gulf, while most of the West African pickings were snapped up by East Coast refiners, with just a few hitting the Gulf.
The WTI/Brent spread for August was around $1.25-35 a barrel, up around five cents from late Friday but still low enough to discourage transatlantic trade.

Meanwhile, the latest chapter in the renewal of Iraqi's oil-for-food deal gave the market a bearish hue on Monday. According to U.N. officials and Western diplomats, the U.N. sanctions committee will allow Baghdad to pump its $2.14 billion sales quota under the renewed accord in a condensed time period, driving export volumes higher once sales resume as expected in July.

Since Iraq has not signed any new sales contracts, nor lifted any oil since the second phase of the deal came into effect on June 8, there is a possibility that the $1 billion limit for each 90 days will be changed.
In Latin America, a U.S. East Coast refiner picked up two cargoes of gasoline-rich Cusiana crude from Colombia's state oil company Ecopetrol for around $1.35 under September WTI fob.
The cargoes will be co-loaded in the last decade of July.
Ecopetrol also sold a cargo of Cano Limon to Petrotrin, the state oil company of Trinidad and Tobago, for an unconfirmed discount of $2.50-55 a barrel to WTI/Cushing.
Still available is a Cusiana cargo loading July 30-August 1.
